title: Introduce staged pager annealing and noise attenuation for SLO burn alerts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Following the capacity regression on 2026-02-24 that produced sustained burn spikes and a surge of duplicate burn-rate pages across services, this ticket implements a graduated "annealing" approach to SLO burn paging plus multiple noise-attenuation controls. The goal is to reduce noisy pages while preserving timely notification for sustained customer-impacting degradations. This is a follow-up to the postmortem: we must combine short-term operational safeguards (patient windows + aggregation) with medium-term signal improvements (impact-weighted burn, alert enrichment) and rollout gates for safety.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce production P1 pager volume from burn-rate alerts by >= 60% for transient spikes (<3m) in the pilot group without increasing time-to-ack for sustained burns (>10m).
Introduce a configurable annealing schedule per service tier (free, standard, enterprise) and ensure default settings are safe for high-impact customers.
Add metadata to burn alerts to enable de-duplication (region, route, model, customer_tier, root_cause_hint).
Provide a rollback toggle and circuit-breaker for the annealing feature that can be flipped from Console within 1 minute.
Dashboard and SLO regression alerting added to track: pager count, mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), time-to-remedy for sustained burns, and false suppression rate.
rollout_plan: 1) Lab: unit/integration tests + synthetic burn simulation (ongoing) - target completion 2026-03-10.
2) Canary: enable on non-critical infra namespaces (staging-like) and one low-traffic prod region for 72h with close monitoring.
3) Pilot: enable for a subset of customer-facing services (route A/B) across three regions for 7 days; collect MTTA and suppression metrics.
4) Ramp: expand to 50% of traffic over 3 days if pilot metrics meet acceptance criteria; otherwise iterate on thresholds.
5) Global: roll to all services with default annealing schedule and allow customer-tier overrides in Console.
implementation_notes: Introduce a new 'annealing' state machine for burn alerts: initial hold -> soft-page -> hard-page if burn persists, with exponential backoff on successive short spikes.
Add 'impact weight' computation at alert generation time: combine customer_tier, active sessions, and %requests failing to produce a burn score to bias immediate paging for high-impact events.
Aggregate burn signals across logical topologies (model+route+region) with a 60s sliding window to avoid duplicate pages for the same root cause.
Emit a structured 'alert_context' JSON blob as a string field that includes hints for runbook automation and de-duplication. Keep payload size bounded.
Console: expose per-service annealing config, preview expected suppressions, and a hard-override feature for support/ops.
testing_plan: Unit tests for annealing state transitions and backoff math.
Integration tests simulating intermittent vs sustained burns with time-acceleration in CI.
Chaos experiments: simulate autoscaler flaps and confirm annealing prevents alert cascades without hiding real outages.
Manual runbook drill with oncall team to validate notices and rollback behavior.
observability_metrics: pager_count_by_alert_type: count(burn_alert) grouped by region, route, model, customer_tier.
suppression_rate: fraction of generated burn signals that resulted in suppressed pages.
mtta_burn_after_annealing: mean time to acknowledge for burn incidents where annealing was applied.
false_suppression_rate: count of suppressed incidents that later meet sustained-burn criteria / total suppressed.
slo_retrogression_delta: change in SLO breach time attributed to annealing.
